title: Validator and Repair Effects Under Shared-Initial-Candidate Semantics: A Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that measured the effect of applying a deterministic validator plus an allowed single repair step to the same sampled LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics) in a guarded NetOps pipeline. The preregistered design targeted retrieval-augmentation (RAG) poisoning, but the executed adapter contract disabled retrievals (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); consequently the realized estimand compares baseline single-shot validator outcomes on a shared sampled candidate against final guarded outcomes (validator ± permitted repair) on that same candidate. On N = 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 judged every sampled initial candidate valid (n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0). No repairs were applied, so baseline and guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rates were identical (1.0). Mapping actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run; we reconcile archived artifacts, quantify the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0), and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limitations with artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-up preregistered experiments.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and scope. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to automate NetOps workflows (intent→configuration translation, staged maintenance, zero-touch configuration), but unconstrained model outputs can violate operational invariants (ordering, reachability, policy constraints). A common mitigation architecture is a guarded pipeline: generation → deterministic validation → bounded repair. Prior surveys and applied work document both the promise of LLM-driven automation and persistent risks from hallucination or translation errors that threaten operational correctness [https://openalex.org/W4406137434, https://openalex.org/W4402742293, https://openalex.org/W4403635865]. These prior records motivate rigorous, artifact-backed experiments that evaluate whether deterministic validators and limited repairs measurably reduce actionable misconfigurations under adversarial or noisy grounding (e.g., poisoned retrievals in RAG pipelines).

Preregistration and realized estimand. We preregistered study candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to evaluate whether targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) increases actionable-misconfiguration rates and whether deterministic defenses reduce that effect. The preregistration defined a paired confirmatory design (N = 250 tasks), a primary poison fraction = 0.30, and a primary estimand: the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded minus baseline) under shared task instances. The executed adapter contract, however, set generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation = false (artifact-backed; see execution/model_configuration.json sha256 a40e96e212ab87da...). Under the executed semantics each task produced exactly one sampled candidate that was reused by both baseline and guarded arms; therefore the comparison measures baseline single-shot validator outcome on that sampled candidate vs. the final guarded outcome (validator ± allowed repair) on the same candidate. This manuscript reports the artifact-grounded outcomes for that realized estimand and documents the preregistration-to-execution reconciliation.
sections.related_work:
Prior surveys and benchmarks. Recent surveys and systems work (2024–2026) document multiple approaches for LLM-driven NetOps and repeatedly recommend deterministic validators or tool augmentation to reduce factual and constraint violations [https://openalex.org/W4406137434, https://openalex.org/W4402742293, https://openalex.org/W4403635865]. Benchmark efforts (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench) provide task banks and primitives but expose construct-validity concerns for operational invariants such as reachability and policy compliance [https://openalex.org/W4399629579].

Tool-augmented pipelines and adversarial findings. Tool-augmented pipelines and RAG architectures are proposed to improve grounding; adjacent-domain adversarial and RAG-poisoning studies (security operations, code translation) show concrete failure modes that motivate controlled poisoning experiments for NetOps [10.20944/preprints202512.0913.v1, https://openalex.org/W4389518608]. However, supplied records commonly present proposals, demonstrations, or limited evaluations rather than broad, topology-grounded empirical measurements of RAG-poisoning effects. Our preregistration targeted that gap; the executed run realized a distinct estimand because retrievals were disabled at execution time.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration summary. The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: ebfbe67f56b5cfb4f0cdbf5a207c7cc095679771ab99515fa8d7d47b2f5e51e3). Primary confirmatory hypothesis H1 expected an absolute paired increase in actionable-misconfig rate at poison_fraction = 0.30; power was calibrated assuming baseline actionable-misconfig ≈ 0.05 for N = 250 (see preregistration for sensitivity analyses).

Executed adapter contract (artifact-backed runtime fields). The archived adapter family and model configuration show the exact executed contract: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini; planned_episode_count = 500; completed_episode_count = 500; model_calls_used = 250; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; retrieval_augmented_generation = false. The execution manifest and model_configuration.json are archived (execution/model_configuration.json sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Crucial explicit statements required by reviewers: (a) exactly one initial sample per task was taken and reused across baseline and guarded conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics), i.e., the baseline and guarded arms began from the identical sampled candidate (this is an execution-time fact, not a modeling choice), and (b) model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0.

Sampling semantics and estimand reconciliation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the only mechanism by which guarded can differ from baseline is validator-triggered repair applied to that same sampled candidate. The paired per-task outcome is actionable_misconfig ∈ {0,1} defined as 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION where VALID_CONFIGURATION is the validator's binary judgment archived per episode (execution/scoring/*.json). Because retrievals were disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not executed; we explicitly document that deviation here and reference the model_configuration.json artifact above.

Validator, tasks, and repairs (artifact-grounded). Task bank: 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; representative tasks and reference answers are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; examples include task-000004 reference sha256 c8b7cf48...). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 produced per-episode VALID_CONFIGURATION judgments and detailed validator_traces archived under execution/scoring/*.json. Repair policy: at most one repair call per failing candidate; repair traces are present in the archive when applied, but for this run repair_provider_trace fields are null because no repairs were invoked.

Statistical analysis plan (executed). Primary confirmatory test executed exactly as preregistered for the realized estimand: exact McNemar two-sided test for paired binary outcomes (α = 0.05) plus paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI via 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Analysis executor recorded: paired_binary_analysis_v1; analysis artifacts archived under analysis/ with hashes recorded.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed). The run started 2026-08-31T21:04:12Z and completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56Z (execution manifest). Planned episodes 500 (two conditions × 250 tasks) completed with failed_episode_count = 0. The model_configuration.json (sha256 a40e96e2...) includes declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and temperature = null (unset).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed numbers). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; sha256 1be58d8255423172b413b0f4908ac22bbf6527870fca0fd3dfa0d5908c987058) records n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0; guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0. Under actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION this yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms and paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts and logs (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl sha256 f36cac00...) confirm these computations.

Representative episode diagnostics. Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json and task-000004-guarded.json; shared_initial_candidate response sha256 2d39d60d...) show identical shared_initial_candidate content across baseline and guarded arms and validator_traces with validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false. No repair_provider_trace entries exist because repairs were never triggered. The deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms provider_call_audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 250 and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false, consistent with a single shared generation per task.

Power and assumption mismatch. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline actionable-misconfig ≈ 0.05; the observed baseline = 0.0 violates that assumption and renders the executed run insensitive to the originally preregistered RAG-poisoning effect sizes. This mismatch is artifact-grounded in the analysis artifacts named above; we report it explicitly rather than retrofitting confirmatory claims.
sections.discussion:
What the realized null result means. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics and the deterministic validator used, every sampled candidate satisfied the validator's rules for the synthetic task bank; consequently the guarded pipeline (validator ± allowed repair) could not change any paired outcome. In other words, when initial candidates are already validator-valid, a bounded repair step that triggers only on validator failures cannot improve paired validity.

What the realized null does not mean. These results do not imply that guarded pipelines are unnecessary in general. The experiment did not exercise retrieval-augmented generation (retrieval_augmented_generation = false), did not permit independent per-condition generation variability, used a single declared LLM and validator, and used synthetic deterministic tasks; therefore the experiment cannot adjudicate the preregistered RAG-poisoning hypotheses nor generalize to production deployments, vendor-specific behavior, or alternative sampling regimes.

Reconciliation of archived metadata and reviewer concern. A reviewer observed that archived analysis_results metadata recorded deviations_from_preregistration = [] while the executed contract disabled retrievals. We reconcile this by explicitly documenting the execution-time facts: the run adhered to the executed adapter contract archived in execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) which set retrieval_augmented_generation = false; the preregistration (sha256 ebfbe67f56b5cfb4f0cdbf5a207c7cc095679771ab99515fa8d7d47b2f5e51e3) described the conceptual RAG plan. Because the executed contract differs from the conceptual plan, the run produced results under the executed semantics and we document that execution-time realization here with explicit artifact references. The archive remains the single source of truth for execution semantics.

Operational and methodological implications for follow-up runs. To test the original RAG-poisoning estimand requires: (1) enabling retrieval_augmented_generation and deterministic poison injection with provenance tagging, (2) permitting independent per-condition generation (generation_semantics != shared_initial_candidate) so the baseline and defended arms can receive different sampled candidates, (3) constructing a provenance-flagged synthetic-poison corpus and containment checks (pre-export hash allowlist), (4) broadening validators to vendor-aware simulators where possible, and (5) optionally testing multiple LLM sampling regimes and temperatures. These concrete steps follow directly from the archived artifacts and the preregistration plan and should be encoded in a follow-up preregistration prior to execution.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (declared model gpt-5-mini; validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5; retrieval disabled). All 250 shared sampled candidates passed deterministic validation (n11 = 250); no repairs were applied and the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate is 0.0 (McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run; we reconciled this execution-time realization against the archived preregistration and execution artifacts and presented artifact-grounded recommendations for a follow-up run that would exercise the original RAG/poisoning estimand.

limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as an execution-time realization documented in execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e2...) and the execution manifest.

The stored scorer semantics required explicit mapping to the preregistered estimand: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 corresponds to no actionable misconfiguration, hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This mapping was applied consistently in all reported analyses.

A single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
